title: Teaching Earl Palmer, Frank Mitchell, Milton Batiste and Melvin Lastie
summary: Students including Earl Palmer and Frank Mitchell, who became his student; Willie Humphrey, Milton Batiste.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I mean, who were some of the students that you taught at Grimmaulds? Now, most of the guys that I taught, I
never would tell anybody that I was a teacher because they played in bands with me and someone
was older than I had. They never would tell anybody that I was a teacher because they would play in bands with me and someone was older than I. And did you ever hear a drummer named Earl Palmer?

Yeah. Well Earl was in my harmony class and he was in my sight singing class. And I would teach them how to read rhythms. And he was very good at it. But I was the only one at the school who was teaching rhythms. You know like they would teach the rhythm along with the melody. But they depend upon the ear. But when you're reading rhythm you're not making any notes, you're just playing the rhythm. He was one of my best students. Then a guy named Frank Mitchell, who was a trumpet player, when he went over there and he found out the money that they were going to pay him, and he told me, man why don't you come over to Brunewald man and sign up and you're getting ninety dollars a month. I said no, I'm doing okay. So he, they needed a trumpet teacher upstairs, you know, because he was segregated. The whites would be downstairs, the blacks would be upstairs. But they needed a trumpet player for him to teach upstairs, so somebody recommended me. So I got the job. So Frank told me, hey man, they finally got you over here, who's your trumpet teacher? I said, well I'm the trumpet teacher. You're the trumpet, man I ain't take no lesson from you. I said, I'm not taking, so I said, okay, you don't have to take lessons from me. So he went, he said whenever you take a lesson you sign for it. So he told Willie Humphrey, who was the teacher over there, Willie Humphrey.

He said, look man, look, I don't want Wallace to teach me anything. You don't know what to teach me. So I'm just going to sign your slip that I'm taking a lesson. He wasn't taking a lesson from Willie either. He just signed a slip. So one day I didn't have any students. I went in one of those little practice rooms and had my Auburn Method. And I was playing some triple tonguing and double tonguing exercises. I heard somebody knock at the door. I said, who is it? Hey man, this is Frank. Who's in there playing that kind of stuff? I said, this is Wallace. Can I come in? I said, yeah. I opened it. Man, what kind of stuff is that you playing on your own? I said, well I've been playing these etudes out of this book, triple tonguing and double. How you do that? Look man, look, I'm going into the office and have my schedule changed. I want you to be my teacher. So I got to be his teacher. And he did all right. He started practicing his song. He said, man, Frank Mitchell told me that you'd run some kind of funny stuff on the horn. He said, how you do that? He said, man, Frank Mitchell told me that you'd run some kind of funny stuff on the horn. How you do that? He said, man, look, can you teach me how to do that? And man before I had to build one horn to build one horn to build one horn to build one to build one horn to build Joe Snider. Snider? No, Snider. Snider. He said, man, Frank Mitchell told me that you'd run some kind of funny stuff on the horn. How you do that? I said, man, look, can you teach me how to do that? And man, before I knew it, I had all the trumpet teachers, I mean all the trumpet students around to take lessons with me. And guys, and I'll tell you another guy was one of my students. He was too young to go to the school and have the government, because he didn't go to the service. It was Milton Baptiste. I started them all.
Milton, okay. Baptiste. Did, I'm thinking of another one, Melvin Lasty.
I taught him too. You taught Melvin? Yeah, Melvin used to come to my house for private lessons.
But he wasn't at Groomwalls? No.
